keyword: google review strategy that actually works
angle: A step-by-step system for earning, responding to, and leveraging Google reviews so local businesses convert more searchers into paying customers.
secondary_kw: how to get more Google reviews

stats.claim: 97% of consumers read online reviews when making local business decisions, and 41% say they always read reviews before choosing a business — up sharply from 29% in 2025.
68% of consumers now require a business to have at least a 4-star rating before they will use it, and 31% specifically require 4.5 stars or higher — both figures significantly higher than in 2025.
74% of consumers only trust reviews written within the last 3 months, and 32% want reviews no older than two weeks — making review recency a critical trust signal.
47% of consumers will not use a business that has fewer than 20 reviews, signaling that review volume is a hard threshold for credibility.
A one-star increase in a business's Yelp rating leads to a 5–9% increase in revenue, driven primarily by independent (non-chain) businesses where online reputation substitutes for brand familiarity.
stats.source_name: Harvard Business School — Michael Luca, "Reviews, Reputation, and Revenue: The Case of Yelp.com"

stats.claim: Businesses that respond to at least 25% of their reviews average 35% more revenue than businesses that do not respond, yet only about 5% of businesses actively respond to their reviews.
